    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    source_dfs.append(df)

# Since there is only one source table and its schema matches the target schema exactly,
# the transformation is straightforward: just ensure the 'value' column is float type.

# Convert 'value' column to float for all source dataframes (only one here)

    source_dfs[i]['value'] = source_dfs[i]['value'].astype(float)

# Union all source tables (only one here, so just take it)

# Reorder columns to match target schema explicitly (day, metric, value)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_90/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_90/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Since only Source2_90_0 is given in the problem, but the operation requires multiple sources,
# we assume Source2_90_1 exists similarly (otherwise, union is trivial).
# If only one source is given, union is just that source.

# Union the two sources (both have same schema)
union_df = pd.concat([source0, source1], ignore_index=True)

# Group by 'day' and 'metric' and sum the 'value' column
result = union_df.groupby(['day', 'metric'], as_index=False).agg({'value': 'sum'})

# Write output
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_90/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
